title: Review of c02's FCH chemoton: S, I and the self-made K layer replicate on seeds 7-8; a new local K-ablation fork shows the vesicle's own catalyst holds its size (seed 7: 39% left vs fed twin 107%), but E is by construction and K spreads between touching bilayers
summary: Re-ran the claimed world and its feed-cut fork on fresh seeds 7 and 8, and added a local catalyst ablation: K erased inside one vesicle at t=300 with a fed twin. Bilayer bodies form from noise and persist; autocatalytic K lives in beads on 1-2 bodies per seed (membrane-like on seed 7 #9 and seed 8 #3). Feed cut kills all K by t~360 and shrinks bodies to micelles (amphiphile -91/-92%) while fed twins keep theirs. The K-cut vesicle shrinks to 39% on seed 7; on seed 8 K re-invades from a touching strip and the vesicle recovers to 86%. Supported for S, I, B; E holds but by construction (amphiphile made only from the fed precursor).

seeds_run.result: pass: fed vesicles persist with K layer; starve twin shrinks to micelles; local K cut shrinks the target to 39%
pass with caveat: K mostly on open strips; starve twin shrinks to micelles; local K cut re-invaded from a touching strip, target 83% -> 86%

verdicts.limitation: E is by construction (amphiphile made only by r K P from the fed precursor, decay everywhere). K-free rings persist through the fed run on amphiphile shared through the bath, and starved bodies become micelles rather than vanishing. K is beaded, carried by only 1-2 of ~5 bodies per seed, aggregate K not membrane-like on my seeds, and K re-invades a cut vesicle from a touching strip (seed 8). No resolution test, no Laplacian twin.
